skill.name: marketing-strategy-pmm
skill.description: Product marketing strategy playbook for B2B SaaS teams. It covers ICP definition, positioning, launch planning, competitive intelligence, sales enablement, and international GTM.
skill.summary: Plan B2B SaaS positioning, launches, competitive intelligence, and sales enablement.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: All external command findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences or inline template markers, not executable Ruby or shell code. The system and network reconnaissance hits are marketing strategy phrases about funding, paid campaigns, launch awareness, and buyer research. No evidence found of prompt injection, data exfiltration, credential access, or runnable code in the scanned SKILL.md.

static_findings.snippet: Template: `[Product] helps [Target Customer] [Achieve Goal] by [Unique Approach]`
Expert Product Marketing playbook for Series A+ startups expanding internationally with hybrid PLG/S
- Funding stage: Seed to Growth (avoid pre-product)
- "Why did you choose us over [Competitor]?"
3. **Customer interviews**: Ask "What alternatives did you consider?"
- What alternatives did you evaluate?
- Why did you choose us over [Competitor]?
- Who did you choose instead? Why?
- What did we do well in the sales process?
**Hybrid (PLG + Sales)**:
- Bottom-up (PLG): Free trial → Paid team plan → Upgrade to Enterprise

- [ ] Paid ads go live (awareness campaigns)
- [ ] Analyze win/loss data (why did we win/lose?)
- Paid ads (Google + LinkedIn) targeting US companies
- Activities: Press release, webinar, email series, paid ads, sales blitz
- [ ] Launch paid ad campaigns (LinkedIn, Google)
- [ ] Increase paid ad spend (ramp up)
- [ ] Paid ads at full budget
- [ ] Win/loss analysis (why did we win/lose deals?)
Week 1: Awareness
- Audience: Existing customers + new prospects + press

content.value_statement: Marketing teams often struggle to connect positioning, launch work, and sales enablement. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured PMM playbooks for B2B SaaS growth.
actual_capabilities: Defines ICPs, buyer personas, segmentation criteria, and validation checks for B2B SaaS markets.
Applies April Dunford positioning steps to value propositions, messaging hierarchy, and proof points.
Creates competitive battlecard structures and win/loss interview workflows.
Plans 90-day GTM launches with channel setup, campaign actions, and success metrics.
Outlines international market entry priorities for the US, UK, DACH, France, and Canada.
Connects PMM work to HubSpot reporting, sales enablement assets, and QBR metrics.
limitations: It is a guidance playbook and does not fetch live competitor or market data.
It does not replace customer interviews, CRM analysis, or legal review.
The scanned package only contains SKILL.md, so referenced assets and scripts are not included.
Examples use placeholder metrics that must be validated against real business data.

use_cases.title: Create Launch Positioning
use_cases.description: Create positioning, messaging hierarchy, competitive battlecards, and launch plans for a new B2B SaaS product.

use_cases.title: Align Growth Strategy
use_cases.description: Align GTM priorities, market entry plans, campaign budgets, and reporting metrics for Series A growth.

use_cases.title: Enable Sales Teams
use_cases.description: Turn positioning and win/loss insights into sales decks, talk tracks, demo flows, and objection handling.

prompt_templates.title: Define a Starter ICP
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me define an ICP for a B2B SaaS product. Ask for missing context, then create firmographic, technographic, and buyer persona details.

prompt_templates.title: Build Positioning and Messaging
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the April Dunford method to position my product. Include alternatives, unique attributes, value, best-fit customers, category, and messaging hierarchy.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a 90-Day Launch
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 90-day GTM launch plan for my product. Include pre-launch work, launch week actions, post-launch optimization, owners, channels, and metrics.

prompt_templates.title: Design International GTM
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an international market entry plan for US, UK, DACH, France, and Canada. Include sequencing, localization, budget allocation, risks, and sales enablement.

output_examples.input: Help define our ICP for a Series A B2B SaaS analytics platform.
output_examples.output: A concise ICP profile with company size, industry, geography, buyer roles, pain level, buying triggers, and validation checks.

output_examples.input: Create launch messaging for our new workflow automation feature.
output_examples.output: A value proposition, benefit hierarchy, persona-specific messages, proof points, and launch metrics for sales and marketing teams.

output_examples.input: Build a battlecard against our main competitor.
output_examples.output: A competitor overview, strengths, weaknesses, our advantages, objection responses, proof points, and sales guidance.

best_practices: Provide product stage, target market, ACV, sales motion, and current customer evidence before asking for strategy.
Validate recommendations with customer interviews, CRM data, sales calls, and campaign performance.
Refresh positioning, battlecards, and launch metrics after each major release or market shift.
anti_patterns: Do not request a complete GTM plan without product, market, and customer context.
Do not treat template metrics as final forecasts without local validation.
Do not use competitive claims externally until legal, product, and sales teams review them.

faq.question: What does this skill help me create?
faq.answer: It helps create ICPs, positioning, launch plans, competitive battlecards, sales assets, and PMM reporting frameworks.

faq.question: Can it replace market research?
faq.answer: No. It structures market research, but users must provide real customer, competitor, and CRM data.

faq.question: Does it run scripts or access tools?
faq.answer: No. The scanned skill is a Markdown playbook and does not include executable files.

faq.question: Which teams benefit most?
faq.answer: Product marketing, growth, demand generation, sales enablement, and marketing leadership teams benefit most.

faq.question: Can it support international expansion?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes market entry guidance for the US, UK, DACH, France, and Canada.

faq.question: How should I provide context?
faq.answer: Share product category, target users, current customers, competitors, pricing, sales motion, and launch goals.
